packages.title: Domestic RHI closed-to-new-applicants QA
facts: Ofgem states the Domestic RHI closed to new applicants on 31 March 2022.
Later annual reports therefore describe continuing scheme administration and payments rather than new scheme entry.
Closure date must be separated from later reporting dates.
Scheme participation is not evidence of current parcel emissions.
No new-applicant count is inferred after closure.

packages.title: Domestic RHI expected-heat QA
facts: Ofgem describes eligible systems receiving payments for low-carbon heat they were expected to produce.
Expected heat is not automatically the same as metered realised heat.
The scheme covers eligible low-carbon heating technologies under its rules.
Expected output must not be relabelled measured energy without supporting evidence.
No parcel heat value is inferred.

packages.title: Domestic RHI payment versus emissions QA
facts: Domestic RHI provides quarterly payments over the scheme payment period for eligible installations.
A payment amount is a financial measure rather than a greenhouse-gas measurement.
Payment status does not establish actual avoided emissions.
Financial and energy metrics must remain separated.
No parcel CO2e value is calculated from payments.

packages.title: Heat-pump deployment 45 kW scope QA
facts: DESNZ heat-pump deployment statistics monitor hydronic heat pumps with capacity up to 45 kW.
The series includes air-source and ground-source heat pumps.
The published data provide installation counts.
Capacity scope must be retained when comparing with other heat-pump sources.
Installation count is not parcel greenhouse-gas emissions.

packages.title: Heat-pump statistics-in-development QA
facts: The March 2026 heat-pump deployment release is published as official statistics in development.
DESNZ states the series is new and remains under methodological development.
The statistics may be revised in future.
Development status must be retained in downstream evidence.
No false finality is assigned to the counts.

packages.title: Heat-pump installation count versus GHG QA
facts: Heat-pump deployment tables provide counts of installations.
An installation count does not quantify electricity consumed by the system.
Installation count does not quantify displaced fuel without additional data.
Therefore deployment counts are not measured avoided greenhouse-gas emissions.
No parcel emissions reduction is inferred.

packages.title: LCREE 2024 turnover £77.0 billion QA
facts: ONS estimates UK low-carbon and renewable-energy-economy turnover at £77.0 billion in 2024.
The estimate is in current prices.
ONS reports an £8.1 billion or 11.8% increase from 2023.
Turnover is an economic statistic rather than an emissions statistic.
No parcel emissions value is inferred from turnover.

packages.title: LCREE 2024 employment 304,000 FTE QA
facts: ONS estimates LCREE employment at 304,000 full-time equivalents in 2024.
ONS reports this was 13,000 FTE or 4.1% lower than 2023.
FTE is an employment measure rather than a count of physical installations.
Employment is not greenhouse-gas emissions evidence.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: LCREE low-carbon electricity £33.6 billion QA
facts: ONS reports the low-carbon electricity group had the highest LCREE turnover in 2024 at £33.6 billion.
This represented 43.7% of total LCREE turnover.
The grouping is an economic activity classification.
Economic turnover must not be interpreted as electricity generation or emissions avoided.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: LCREE low-emission vehicle turnover-growth QA
facts: ONS reports the low-emission vehicles and infrastructure group had the largest percentage turnover increase from 2023 to 2024.
The reported increase was 33.8%, from £8.7 billion to £11.6 billion.
Turnover growth is not vehicle registration growth.
It is not a direct emissions-reduction measure.
No parcel inference is made.

packages.title: LCREE 25,000-business sample QA
facts: The LCREE Survey QMI states the data collection uses a sample of 25,000 businesses.
The survey has UK geographic coverage.
The survey is annual.
Sample-based estimates are not a census of every business.
No individual-site emissions are inferred from the survey sample.

packages.title: LCREE survey uncertainty QA
facts: ONS states LCREE estimates are survey-based and subject to sampling uncertainty.
Confidence intervals are used to express statistical accuracy.
Sector estimates can have greater uncertainty than combined groups.
Central estimates must not be treated as exact population measurements.
No parcel precision is inferred from survey estimates.

packages.title: LCREE indirect 2024 provisional QA
facts: ONS publishes separate LCREE indirect and total estimates as official statistics in development.
The 2024 indirect estimates are provisional because they use 2023 UK input-output analytical tables.
Direct and indirect estimates must remain distinct.
Provisional status must be retained in downstream use.
No emissions value is inferred from indirect economic activity.

packages.title: LCREE indirect double-counting caution QA
facts: ONS notes further methodological work is needed for LCREE indirect estimates.
The methodology uses proxies in some areas.
Potential double counting may bias estimates upward.
Indirect estimates therefore require explicit quality caution.
No economic estimate is converted into parcel emissions.

packages.title: Final UK GHG source end-user SIC release QA
facts: The DESNZ final UK greenhouse-gas dataset provides territorial estimates going back to 1990.
Final estimates are presented by source in February each year.
They are updated in March to include end-user estimates.
They are updated in June to include Standard Industrial Classification estimates.
Source, end-user and SIC views must not be conflated.

packages.title: Final UK GHG territorial-scope QA
facts: DESNZ final UK greenhouse-gas statistics cover emissions occurring within UK borders.
This is a territorial accounting scope.
Territorial figures differ conceptually from residence and consumption-footprint measures.
National territorial totals do not identify individual property emissions.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: LCREE economic activity versus GHG QA
facts: LCREE statistics measure economic activity such as turnover, employment, trade and business counts.
The LCREE definition covers activities likely to help generate lower greenhouse-gas emissions.
Economic activity is not itself a measured greenhouse-gas outcome.
Growth in a low-carbon sector cannot be converted directly into avoided CO2e without additional evidence.
No parcel emissions benefit is inferred.

packages.title: Cross-source parcel inference guard 108 QA
facts: Batch 108 sources operate at national, industry, facility, scheme, monitoring-station or survey levels.
None of the reviewed sources provides a verified cadastral parcel binding for this slot.
Activity, factors, concentrations, economic estimates and inventories remain in their published semantic categories.
Cross-source arithmetic is blocked where units, geography or accounting bases are incompatible.
Parcel binding and measured parcel values remain zero until a separate verified geometry-and-source gate passes.
